where p is the trainer, q the sampler, A_i the (group-centred) advantage of rollout i, h_it the prefix and N the number of completion tokens. Its gradient is an estimate of

but the policy gradient is E_{x~p}[ A * grad log p(x) ]. The two differ whenever q != p, and the difference is not zero-mean noise. The expected gradient on the logits at context h is

    U(h)  = sum_x q(x) Q(h,x) (e_x - p)          (what the code estimates)
    T(h)  = sum_x p(x) Q(h,x) (e_x - p)          (the true gradient)

Let Qbar be any constant. Since sum_x (e_x - p) = 0 in the sense sum_x p(x)(e_x - p) = 0, the constant part of Q contributes exactly zero to T, but not to U:

    U - T = Qbar (q - p) + (first order in the variation delta(x) = Q(h,x) - Qbar) * (q - p).

So the uncorrected loss contains a systematic term Qbar * (q - p) per context. If the mean advantage E[A | h] is positive at a context, the update pulls p toward q there; if negative, it pushes p away from q. Group-centring makes the advantage average zero over a group, but not per prefix: E[A | h] is large at the answer positions, where the prefix already determines most of the outcome. Why it compounds and collapses: q is refreshed from p every step, so the bias is applied again to a new q. With plus/minus rewards most rollouts are unsolved (A = -1), and the bias Qbar (q - p) with Qbar < 0 moves mass toward the mode of p, which is sharpening.     U_cen(h) = sum_x q(x) Q(h,x) (e_x - q),
    U_cen - T = sum_x (q - p)(x) delta(x) e_x - (sum_x q delta) q + (sum_x p delta) p,

with delta = Q - Qbar. The constant-advantage bias Qbar (q - p) is gone exactly. What remains is proportional to the variation delta of the advantage across tokens at the same context, times the mismatch q - p. This is second order in the mismatch: it needs both a mismatch and an advantage that varies with the token choice, which is what learning is for. Group centring cannot remove the per-prefix mean; the centring of the score does.

Why this uses no IS weight: the centring replaces the weight by a zero-mean baseline built from q, which the sampler already provides. It does not need p/q, so it does not inherit the variance of IS, and it is exact in expectation for any q, including stale weights, quantised weights and quantised KV caches, because it only uses the sampler distribution that was actually used for sampling.
